options: A community plus its nonliving surroundings
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes the living community PLUS the nonliving surroundings (water, soil, sunlight, climate) in an area.
questions.misconception: Community = living only. The ecosystem adds the nonliving surroundings to that community.

questions.prompt: How does energy typically move through an ecosystem?
options: From the sun to plants to animals
questions.explanation: Energy enters ecosystems as sunlight, is captured by plants, then passes to animals that eat them.
questions.misconception: Energy flows one direction (sun -> plants -> animals); it is matter, not energy, that cycles.

questions.prompt: How is matter (materials) recycled in an ecosystem?
options: Decomposers return dead materials to the soil
Rocks make new soil from nothing
questions.explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria break down dead organisms, returning nutrients to the soil for plants to reuse.
questions.misconception: Matter does not vanish - it is recycled back through the system by decomposers.

questions.prompt: How big can an ecosystem be?
options: From a puddle to a whole desert or forest
Only the size of a house
questions.explanation: Ecosystems come in all sizes - a puddle, a rotting log, a pond, or a vast forest are all ecosystems.
questions.misconception: There is no minimum or fixed size - an ecosystem is defined by its living + nonliving whole.
